questions.prompt: Do you prefer using the internet on your phone or computer?
questions.sampleA2: I like my phone. It is small and I can use it everywhere. But my computer is good too because the screen is bigger.
questions.sampleB1: I think I prefer using the internet on my phone. It's more convenient because I can take it anywhere. For example, I use it on the bus. However, sometimes the computer is better because the screen is bigger, and it's easier to type.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, it really depends on what I'm doing. For quick stuff like checking messages or scrolling through social media, my phone wins hands down because I can just whip it out anywhere. But when it comes to proper work, like writing essays or doing research, I much prefer my laptop. The bigger screen and keyboard make life so much easier.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga telefonim yoqadi. U kichkina va men uni hamma joyda ishlatishim mumkin. Lekin kompyuterim ham yaxshi, chunki ekrani kattaroq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, internetdan telefonda foydalanishni afzal ko'raman. Bu qulayroq, chunki uni istalgan joyga olib ketishim mumkin.
Masalan, men undan avtobusda foydalanaman.
Biroq, ba'zida kompyuter yaxshiroq, chunki ekrani kattaroq va yozish osonroq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Umuman olganda, men ko'pgina kundalik vazifalar uchun internetdan telefonda foydalanishga moyilman. Uning ko'chma ekanligi katta afzallik, bu menga tezda ma'lumotni tekshirish yoki yo'lda aloqa qilish imkonini beradi.

Biroq, hujjatlar yozish yoki batafsil tadqiqot o'tkazish kabi murakkabroq faoliyatga kelganda, men kompyuterni ancha samarali deb bilaman. Katta ekran va to'g'ri klaviatura mening unumdorligim va qulayligimga sezilarli ta'sir qiladi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you prefer using the internet on your phone or computer?
idioms: at one's fingertips - "qo'l ostida (oson yetadigan joyda, ma'lumot qidirish haqida)"
on the go - "yo'l-yo'lakay (harakatlanib yurgan paytda)"
the best of both worlds - "har ikkisining eng yaxshi tomoni (ikkala qurilmaning afzalliklaridan foydalanishni bildiradi)"
sentenceStarters: "I overwhelmingly prefer using my smartphone for internet browsing due to..." - "Men internetga kirish uchun ko'proq smartfonimdan foydalanishni afzal ko'raman, chunki…"
"However, when tackling deep research or drafting professional emails, I..." - "Biroq, chuqur izlanishlar olib borish yohud rasmiy xatlar yozish kabi ishlarda men..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I overwhelmingly prefer using my smartphone for internet browsing due to its unmatched convenience. It allows me to stay connected seamlessly whether I am commuting or grabbing a quick coffee.
However, when tackling deep research or drafting professional emails, I invariably switch to my computer. The larger screen and tactile keyboard make heavy cognitive tasks much more manageable.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men internetda ko‘rish uchun smartfonimdan foydalanishni juda afzal ko‘raman, chunki uning qulayligi beqiyosdir. Bu menga ishga qatnayotganimda yoki shunchaki bir chashka qahva ichayotganimda ham doimiy aloqada bo‘lish imkonini beradi.

Biroq, chuqur tadqiqotlar olib borish yoki professional elektron pochta xabarlarini yozish kerak bo'lganda, men doimo kompyuterimga o'taman. Katta ekran va sezgir klaviatura og'ir kognitiv vazifalarni ancha osonlashtiradi.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually study when you need to focus?
questions.sampleA2:
I study at home.

I like my room because it is quiet.

And I have a desk.
questions.sampleB1:
When I need to focus, I usually study in my room.

I think it's the best place because it's quiet and comfortable.

Sometimes I go to a cafe, but it can be noisy.

So, my room is better for studying.
questions.sampleB2: Well, when I really need to knuckle down, I usually head to my room and shut the door. The thing is, I can't concentrate at all if there's noise around me. Occasionally I'll go to the library if I want a change of scenery, but nine times out of ten my desk at home does the trick.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men odatda uyda o'qiyman.

Menga o'z xonam yoqadi, chunki u yerda tinch.

Va menda stol bor.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Diqqatni jamlashim kerak bo'lganda, odatda o'z xonamda o'qiyman.

Menimcha, bu eng yaxshi joy, chunki u yer tinch va qulay.

Ba'zan kafega boraman, lekin u yer shovqinli bo'lishi mumkin.

Shunday qilib, o'qish uchun mening xonam yaxshiroq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Agar men diqqatimni jamlashim kerak bo'lsa, odatda tinch muhitda o'qishni afzal ko'raman.

Odatda, bu mening uy ofisimni anglatadi, u yerda men chalg'ituvchi omillarni nazorat qila olaman.

Biroq, ba'zida manzaraning o'zgarishi foydali bo'ladi, shuning uchun men universitet kutubxonasining unchalik gavjum bo'lmagan burchagiga borishim mumkin.

Asosiysi, men xalaqitlarni kamaytiradigan va materialga chinakam kirishadigan joyni topishdir.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Where do you usually study when you need to focus?
idioms: get down to business - "ishga(jiddiy maqsadga) kirishmoq"
hit the books - "kitoblarga yopishmoq (qattiq o'qishni boshlamoq)"
in the zone - "butun diqqati shu ishda bo'lgan o'ta qulay holatda"
phrases: pin-drop silence - "ignadek narsa tushganini ham eshitadigan darajadagi sukunat"
sentenceStarters: "When I require absolute concentration, I typically head straight to…" - "Mengga mutlaq diqqat-e'tibor kerak bo'lganda, men odatda to'g'ri ... ga boraman."
"Alternatively, if the library is closed, I meticulously organize my…" - "Aks holda, agar kutubxona yopiq bo'lsa, men ehtiyotkorlik bilan o'zimning..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
When I require absolute concentration, I typically head straight to the local library. The sheer pin-drop silence and the collective atmosphere of diligent students create the ideal environment for deep work.
Alternatively, if the library is closed, I meticulously organize my bedroom desk into a distraction-free zone. By turning off my phone, I can effectively "get down to business."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men mutlaq diqqatni jamlashim kerak bo'lganda, odatda to'g'ri mahalliy kutubxonaga boraman. U yerdagi mutlaq sukunat va tirishqoq talabalarning umumiy muhiti chuqur ishlash uchun ideal muhit yaratadi.

Yana bir variant, agar kutubxona yopiq bo'lsa, men yotoqxonamdagi stolimni chalg'ituvchi omillardan xoli zonaga aylantirib, sinchkovlik bilan tartibga solaman. Telefonimni o'chirib, men samarali ravishda ishga kirisha olaman.

questions.prompt: What kind of fastfood do you like most?
questions.sampleA2:
I like burgers.

They are tasty and easy to eat.

I like fries too, because they are salty.
questions.sampleB1:
Well, I think I like pizza the most.

It's easy to find and there are many different types.

For example, I like pepperoni pizza and also vegetarian pizza.

It's not very healthy, but it's a good treat sometimes.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose if I had to pick, I'm a bit of a sucker for a good burger. There's something about a juicy patty with melted cheese that I find hard to resist. That said, I try not to overdo it, because deep down I know it's not exactly good for me. So I treat it as a once-in-a-while thing rather than a regular habit.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men burgerlarni yaxshi ko'raman.

Ular mazali va yeyishga oson.

Men kartoshka fri ham yaxshi ko'raman, chunki u sho'r.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, pizza menga ko'proq yoqadi.

Uni topish oson va juda ko'p turli xillari bor.

Masalan, menga pepperoni pizza va vegetarian pizza ham yoqadi.

U juda ham foydali emas, lekin ba'zida yaxshi bir xursandchilik.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Agar tanlashga to'g'ri kelsa, men yaxshi burger yeyishni yoqtiraman derdim, ayniqsa qiziqarli qo'shimchalari bor burgerlarni.

Men arzon fastfud burgerlarining katta muxlisi emasman, lekin yaxshi tayyorlangan burger juda ham qoniqarli bo'lishi mumkin.

Biroq, men fastfudni juda tez-tez yemashga harakat qilaman, chunki u uzoq muddatda siz uchun juda foydali emas.

Shunday qilib, men burgerlarni yoqtirsam ham, bu mening doimiy ovqatlanishimning bir qismi emas, balki vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zimni erkalashimdir.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What kind of fastfood do you like most?
idioms: mouth-watering - "og'iz suvini qochiradigan (juda ishtahaochar)"
once in a blue moon - "juda kamdan-kam (oyda yilda bir marta)"
have a sweet tooth - "shirinlikxo'r bo'lmoq (o'rxin taomlarga emas, bunday turlarga ko'proq ishlatilsada, ifoda keng uchraydi)"
phrases: guilty pleasure - "zararli bo'lsa ham qilinadigan sevimli mashg'ulot (yoki yegulik)"
sentenceStarters: "If I have to choose, I am undoubtedly partial to a..." - "Tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, men, shubhasiz, … ni xush ko'raman."
"However, I am acutely aware of the severe health implications of…" - "Biroq, men … ning sog'liqqa salbiy ta'sirlarini juda yaxshi anglayman."

questions.sampleAnswer:
If I have to choose, I am undoubtedly partial to a good quality gourmet burger paired with crispy fries. When the ingredients are fresh and well-seasoned, it transforms a simple guilty pleasure into a mouth-watering delight.
However, I am acutely aware of the severe health implications of eating junk food, so I strictly limit these indulgences to perhaps once a month, ensuring it remains an "occasional treat."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Agar tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, men, shubhasiz, yaxshi sifatli gurme burgerni qarsildoq kartoshka bilan birga iste'mol qilishni afzal ko'raman. Ingredientlar yangi va yaxshi ziravorlangan bo'lsa, u oddiy aybdor lazzatni og'izni suvga to'ldiradigan rohatga aylantiradi.

Biroq, men tez tayyorlanadigan ovqatlar iste'mol qilishning jiddiy sog'liq uchun oqibatlaridan juda yaxshi xabardorman, shuning uchun men bu zaifliklarni oyiga bir martadan ko'p bo'lmagan holda qat'iy cheklayman va bu "vaqti-vaqti bilan beriladigan lazzat" bo'lib qolishini ta'minlayman.

questions.sampleA1: This is farm. Man work. Vegetables. Good.
questions.sampleA2: I see two pictures. One is a garden on a roof, and one is a big farm. The farm is big, but the garden is small. I like the garden because it is near the city.
questions.sampleB1: Okay, so in the first picture, there's someone growing food on a roof in the city. I think it's a good idea because there isn't much space. In the second picture, there's a farmer in a field. It's a very big farm. Both pictures show people growing food, however, they are very different places.
questions.sampleB2: These two images both depict people engaged in gardening, yet they present quite different contexts. In the first picture, we see a vibrant rooftop garden in what appears to be a bustling city, judging by the distinctive skyline in the background. Several individuals are actively tending to plants in raised beds, suggesting a community or urban farming initiative. On the other hand, the second image focuses on a single woman kneeling down in a much more traditional, perhaps larger, vegetable patch. She's carefully planting seeds in neat rows of freshly tilled soil. While both show the cultivation of food, the first highlights a modern, communal approach, whereas the second evokes a more classic, individual connection to the land and the hard graft of growing produce.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ikkita rasm ko'ryapman. Bittasi tom ustidagi bog', ikkinchisi esa katta ferma. Ferma katta, lekin bog' kichkina. Menga bog' yoqadi, chunki u shaharga yaqin.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda, shaharda tomda kimdir oziq-ovqat yetishtirayotgan odam bor. Menimcha, bu yaxshi fikr, chunki joy unchalik ko'p emas. Ikkinchi rasmda, dalada fermer bor. Bu juda katta ferma. Ikkala rasm ham odamlarning oziq-ovqat yetishtirayotganini ko'rsatadi, ammo ular juda boshqa joylar.
questions.uzSampleB2: Birinchi rasmda shahar bog'i ko'rsatilgan, ehtimol binoning tomida. Kimdir ko'tarilgan to'shaklardagi o'simliklarga g'amxo'rlik qilmoqda. Bu shahar muhitida oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarishning ijodiy usuli kabi ko'rinadi. Ikkinchi rasm esa, aksincha, an'anaviy qishloq xo'jaligi manzaralarini taqdim etadi. U dalada o'sayotgan ekinlari bo'lgan katta fermaga o'xshaydi. Ikkala rasm ham oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarish haqida bo'lsa-da, ular juda xilma-xil miqyos va yondashuvlarni ifodalaydi. Shahar bog'i, ehtimol, shaxsiy foydalanish yoki kichik bir jamoa uchun bo'lsa, ferma, ehtimol, ancha katta bozor uchun oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarmoqda.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe the images
idioms: old world - "eski dunyo (qadimiy urf-odatlar)"
salt of the earth - "yerning tuzi (halol, mehnatkash va ishonchli odamlar - dehqonlarga nisbatan ishlatsa bo'ladi)"
reap what you sow - "nima eksang, shuni o'rasan"
sentenceStarters: "The first picture vividly illustrates a modern approach to agriculture, showing…" - "Birinchi rasmda dehqonchilikka zamonaviy yondashuv yaqqol ko'rsatilgan bo'lib, u yerda..."
"Conversely, the second image depicts a more conventional paradigm. A farmer is…" - "Aksincha, ikkinchi rasm ancha an'anaviy yondoshuvni aks ettiradi. Fermer/Dehqon..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The first picture vividly illustrates a modern approach to agriculture, showing an individual tending to vegetables in wooden planters atop an urban rooftop. It highlights a resourceful utilization of limited concrete space.
Conversely, the second image depicts a more conventional paradigm. A farmer is working in a vast, open field, embodying the time-honored traditions of large-scale cultivation. Together, they juxtapose "old world" rural farming alongside innovative urban sustainability.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasm qishloq xo'jaligiga zamonaviy yondashuvni yaqqol ko'rsatib beradi, unda bir shaxs shahar tomidagi yog'och idishlarda sabzavotlarni parvarish qilmoqda. Unda cheklangan beton maydonidan unumli foydalanish ta'kidlangan.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasm an'anaviyroq paradigmmani aks ettiradi. Fermer keng, ochiq dalada ishlamoqda va keng ko'lamli dehqonchilikning qadimiy an'analarini o'zida mujassam etgan. Ular birgalikda "eski dunyo" qishloq xo'jaligini innovatsion shahar barqarorligi bilan yonma-yon qo'yadi.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of urban gardening?
questions.sampleA1: I like garden. Garden is good. Grow food.
questions.sampleA2: I think urban gardens are good. You can grow food in the city. And it's fun. But it's hard work sometimes because you need to water the plants.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think there are some good things about urban gardening. For example, you can grow your own vegetables, which is healthier. Also, it can make the city look nicer. However, it might be difficult if you don't have much space or time.
questions.sampleB2: Well, there are quite a few upsides, in my view. First off, growing your own veg means you get fresh, chemical-free food right on your doorstep. On top of that, tending to plants is really good for your mental health, it helps you unwind after a long day. And of course, it brings a bit of greenery into an otherwise grey city.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men bog'ni yaxshi ko'raman. Bog' yaxshi. Oziq-ovqat yetishtirish.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, shahar bog'lari yaxshi. Shaharda oziq-ovqat yetishtirishingiz mumkin. Va bu qiziqarli. Lekin ba'zida bu qiyin ish, chunki o'simliklarni sug'orishingiz kerak.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, shahar bog'dorchiligining ba'zi yaxshi tomonlari bor.
Masalan, siz o'zingizning sabzavotlaringizni yetishtirishingiz mumkin, bu esa sog'lomroqdir. Shuningdek, u shaharni yanada chiroyli ko'rsatishi mumkin.
Biroq, agar sizda unchalik ko'p joy yoki vaqt bo'lmasa, bu qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Shahar bog'dorchiligining bir nechta afzalliklari bor,
mening fikrimcha.
Birinchidan, bu odamlarga yangi, mahalliy yetishtirilgan mahsulotlarga kirish imkonini beradi, bu ularning ovqatlanishini yaxshilaydi va sanoat qishloq xo'jaligiga bog'liqlikni kamaytiradi.
Ikkinchidan, shahar bog'lari shaharlarning estetik jozibasini oshirishi, aholining hayot sifatini yaxshilaydigan yashil hududlarni yaratishi mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, u jamiyatning ishtiroki uchun imkoniyatlar yaratadi va atrof-muhit barqarorligini yaxshiroq tushunishga yordam beradi.
Biroq, uning imkoniyatlarini to'liq ro'yobga chiqarish uchun cheklangan joy va tuproqning ifloslanishi kabi muammolarni hal qilish kerak.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Benefits of urban gardening
idioms: the concrete jungle - "beton changalzor (kattakon shaharlarning ta'rifi)"
a green thumb - "yashil barmoqqa ega bo'lmoq (dehqonchilik / gulchilikka uquvli bo'lmoq)"
bear fruit - "hosil bermoq (yaxshi natija bermoq)"
sentenceStarters: "Urban gardening presents a multitude of highly significant benefits for…" - "Shahar bog'dorchiligi (dehqonchilik) shaharliklar uchun ko'plab o'ta muhim afzalliklarni…"
"Furthermore, interacting with nature in a concrete jungle serves as…" - "Bundan tashqari, beton changalzorida tabiat bilan aloqada bo'lish ajoyib... bo'lib xizmat qiladi."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Urban gardening presents a multitude of highly significant benefits for city dwellers. Firstly, it promotes unparalleled environmental sustainability. By growing food on rooftops or balconies, people drastically reduce the carbon footprint associated with transporting produce from rural farms.
Furthermore, interacting with nature in a concrete jungle serves as a phenomenal psychological anchor. Tending to plants is profoundly therapeutic, mitigating the chronic stress caused by the fast-paced urban lifestyle.
Lastly, it guarantees access to absolutely fresh, organic food free from harmful pesticides. Urban gardening proves that you can "bring the country to the city," fostering a deeper appreciation for nature.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shahar bog'dorchiligi shahar aholisi uchun juda muhim bo'lgan ko'plab afzalliklarni taqdim etadi. Birinchidan, u misli ko'rilmagan ekologik barqarorlikni targ'ib qiladi. Odamlar tomlarda yoki balkonlarda oziq-ovqat yetishtirish orqali qishloq xo'jaliklaridan mahsulot tashish bilan bog'liq bo'lgan uglerod izini keskin kamaytiradi.
Bundan tashqari, beton o'rmonda tabiat bilan o'zaro aloqa ajoyib psixologik langar vazifasini o'taydi. O'simliklarga g'amxo'rlik qilish juda terapevtik bo'lib, tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan shahar turmush tarzi keltirib chiqaradigan surunkali stressni kamaytiradi.
Va nihoyat, u zararli pestitsidlardan xoli bo'lgan mutlaqo yangi, organik oziq-ovqatga kirishni kafolatlaydi. Shahar bog'dorchiligi "qishloqni shaharga olib kelish" mumkinligini isbotlaydi va tabiatga chuqurroq minnatdorchilikni uyg'otadi.

questions.prompt: Why is traditional farming still more important?
questions.sampleA1: Farm is good. Food comes from farm. Important!
questions.sampleA2: I think farm is important. It gives us food, and my family eats food. Big farms give lots of food to the shops. I like farms.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think traditional farming is still very important. For example, it gives us a lot of food. Also, many people work on farms, so it gives them jobs. However, it can be hard work, but it's important for food.
questions.sampleB2: The way I see it, traditional farming is still the backbone of our food supply. At the end of the day, you simply can't feed billions of people from rooftops and balconies alone. Big farms produce food on a massive scale, and they keep prices down for ordinary families. So, while urban gardening is lovely, it can't really compete when it comes to sheer volume.
questions.uzSampleA1: Fermer xo'jaligi yaxshi. Oziq-ovqat fermadan keladi. Muhim!
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, dehqonchilik muhim. U bizga oziq-ovqat beradi, va mening oilam oziq-ovqat yeydi. Katta dehqon xo'jaliklari do'konlarga ko'p oziq-ovqat beradi. Menga dehqonchilik yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, an'anaviy dehqonchilik hali ham juda muhim.
Masalan, u bizga juda ko'p oziq-ovqat beradi. Shuningdek, ko'p odamlar fermalarda ishlaydi, shuning uchun u ularga ish o'rinlarini beradi.
Biroq, bu og'ir mehnat bo'lishi mumkin, lekin bu oziq-ovqat uchun muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: An'anaviy dehqonchilik, mening fikrimcha, juda muhim bo'lib qolmoqda, asosan, global miqyosda talab qilinadigan oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarishning katta hajmi tufayli. Zamonaviy texnologiyalar rivojlanayotgan bo'lsa-da, an'anaviy usullar hali ham oziq-ovqat ta'minotining katta qismini ishlab chiqaradi. Bundan tashqari, an'anaviy dehqonchilik ko'pincha qishloq jamoalarini qo'llab-quvvatlaydi va qishloq xo'jaligi merosini saqlaydi. Albatta, ekologik muammolar mavjud, ammo uning oziq-ovqat xavfsizligiga qo'shgan hissasi inkor etib bo'lmaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Importance of traditional farming
idioms: feed the masses - "ommaga ozuqa bermoq (katta xalqni boqmoq)"
salt of the earth - "halol va mehnatkash insonlar"
cash cow - "pul sog'in sigiri (doimiy va ishonchli daromad manbai)"
sentenceStarters: "Despite the rise of urban initiatives, traditional farming remains unequivocally crucial because…" - "Shahar tashabbuslarining ko'payishiga qaramay, an'anaviy dehqonchilik o'zining mutlaqo muhimligini saqlab qoladi, chunki…"
"Moreover, traditional farming forms the economic backbone of countless…" - "Bundan tashqari, an'anaviy dehqonchilik son-sanoqsiz davlatlarning...ni tashkil qiladi."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Despite the rise of urban initiatives, traditional farming remains unequivocally crucial because of its massive scale. The sheer volume of crops required to feed the accelerating global population can only be generated through vast tracts of rural land and industrialized agricultural machinery.
Moreover, traditional farming forms the economic backbone of countless developing nations. It provides essential livelihoods for millions of rural families and is vitally important for international trade and export revenues.
Essentially, while rooftop gardens are undoubtedly charming and beneficial, they cannot "feed the masses." Traditional agriculture will permanently remain the foundation of global food security.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shahar tashabbuslarining ko'payishiga qaramay, an'anaviy dehqonchilik o'zining ulkan miqyosi tufayli shubhasiz muhimligicha qolmoqda. Global aholining tez o'sishi uchun zarur bo'lgan ekinlarning katta hajmi faqat qishloq yerlarining keng maydonlari va sanoatlashgan qishloq xo'jaligi texnikasi orqali ishlab chiqarilishi mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, an'anaviy dehqonchilik ko'plab rivojlanayotgan davlatlarning iqtisodiy asosini tashkil etadi. U millionlab qishloq oilalari uchun muhim tirikchilik manbai bo'lib, xalqaro savdo va eksport daromadlari uchun hayotiy ahamiyatga ega.

Aslida, tom ustidagi bog'lar shubhasiz jozibali va foydali bo'lsa-da, ular "ommaga oziq-ovqat bera olmaydi". An'anaviy qishloq xo'jaligi global oziq-ovqat xavfsizligining asosi bo'lib abadiy qoladi.

questions.prompt: Can you describe an unusual hobby you tried?
questions.sampleA1: Hobby... I try... cook. Is difficult. I like eat.
questions.sampleA2: I tried... uh... origami. It's paper folding. It was hard but fun. I made a bird and a flower. And I stopped because it was too difficult.
questions.sampleB1: An unusual hobby I tried was learning to play the ukulele. I thought it would be easy, but it wasn't as easy as I expected. However, it was quite fun to learn a few simple songs. In my opinion, it's a good hobby for relaxing. I still play sometimes, but not very often.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so an unusual hobby I gave a go to a while back was pottery, throwing clay on a wheel. I'd always assumed it looked dead easy on those videos, but honestly, it was a completely different story once I sat down at the wheel myself. My first few attempts collapsed into a soggy mess, and I ended up covered in mud from head to toe. Still, after a handful of lessons, I finally managed to shape a wonky little bowl, and I was over the moon about it. The whole thing was surprisingly relaxing, because you have to switch off completely and focus on what your hands are doing. As for why trying new hobbies matters, I reckon it's really important for keeping your mind fresh. If you stick to the same old routine day in, day out, you can end up in a bit of a rut. Picking up something new pushes you out of your comfort zone and, more often than not, you discover talents you never knew you had. On top of that, it's a brilliant way to meet like-minded people. When it comes to how people actually find new hobbies, I'd say the internet plays a huge part these days. Platforms like YouTube and TikTok throw endless tutorials at you, so you can dip your toe in without spending a penny. That said, plenty of people still catch the bug from friends or family, tagging along to a class and getting hooked. To be honest, word of mouth is still one of the most powerful ways we stumble upon new passions.

bulletPoints: Can you describe an unusual hobby you tried?
Why is trying new hobbies important in life?
How do people usually explore new hobbies?
questions.sampleAnswer:
An unusual hobby I tried:
An exceptionally quirky hobby I picked up recently is 'magnet fishing.' It involves tossing a powerful neodymium magnet attached to a strong rope into a canal or river to retrieve metallic objects. It is oddly thrilling, acting like an aquatic treasure hunt. While I mostly drag up rusty bicycle tires or old tools, the sheer suspense of not knowing what lies beneath the surface is highly addictive.
Why trying new hobbies is important:
Venturing out to learn new hobbies is paramount because it actively prevents mental stagnation. Repeating the same daily routine can inevitably lead to burnout. Engaging in novel activities forces the brain to build new neural pathways, fostering creative flexibility. It guarantees continuous "personal evolution."
How people usually explore new hobbies:
Nowadays, individuals predominantly discover new passions through the internet. Algorithm-driven platforms like YouTube offer an endless stream of tutorials exposing users to obscure niches. Alternatively, people often adopt hobbies through peer influence, joining clubs or groups initiated by their close friends, proving that curiosity is highly contagious.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men sinab ko'rgan g'ayrioddiy mashg'ulot:
Yaqinda o'zimga olgan juda g'alati mashg'ulot bu "magnit bilan baliq ovlash". Bu kuchli neodim magnitni mustahkam arqonga bog'lab, metall buyumlarni olish uchun kanal yoki daryoga tashlashni o'z ichiga oladi. Bu g'alati darajada hayajonli, suv osti xazina oviga o'xshaydi. Men asosan zanglagan velosiped shinalari yoki eski asboblarni tortib olsam ham, sirt ostida nima borligini bilmaslikning o'zi juda o'ziga tortadi.
Nima uchun yangi mashg'ulotlarni sinab ko'rish muhim:
Yangi mashg'ulotlarni o'rganishga kirishish juda muhim, chunki u aqliy turg'unlikning oldini oladi. Kundalik bir xil tartibni takrorlash muqarrar ravishda charchashga olib kelishi mumkin. Yangi faoliyat bilan shug'ullanish miyani yangi neyron yo'llarini qurishga majbur qiladi va ijodiy moslashuvchanlikni rivojlantiradi. Bu doimiy "shaxsiy evolyutsiya"ni kafolatlaydi.
Odamlar odatda yangi mashg'ulotlarni qanday o'rganadilar:
Hozirgi kunda odamlar asosan internet orqali yangi qiziqishlarini topadilar. YouTube kabi algoritmga asoslangan platformalar foydalanuvchilarni noma'lum sohalar bilan tanishtiradigan cheksiz oqimdagi darsliklarni taklif qiladi. Yoki bo'lmasa, odamlar ko'pincha o'zlarining yaqin do'stlari tashabbusi bilan tuzilgan klublar yoki guruhlarga qo'shilib, tengdoshlar ta'siri orqali mashg'ulotlarni qabul qiladilar, bu qiziquvchanlik juda yuqumli ekanligini isbotlaydi.

questions.prompt: Students should learn financial education at school.
questions.sampleA1: Yes. Money good. I like money. School teach.
questions.sampleA2: I think yes. Money is important. School can teach about money. And then students know. But maybe it is hard.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's a good idea. Learning about money is important for everyone. If students learn about it at school, they will be better prepared for the future. For example, they can learn about saving and budgeting. However, it might be difficult to fit it into the curriculum.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm firmly in favour of teaching financial education in schools, though I can see there are arguments on both sides. On the one hand, those who back the idea point out that far too many young people leave school without the faintest idea of how to budget, save, or steer clear of debt. If we taught teenagers these skills early on, they'd be far better equipped to stand on their own two feet as adults. After all, money troubles can cause an awful lot of stress later in life, so getting to grips with the basics from a young age would surely pay off in the long run. On the other hand, critics do have a point. The school timetable is already crammed to the brim, and squeezing in yet another subject might pile even more pressure on both students and teachers. Some would argue that managing money is really a family matter, and that parents ought to take the lead on it at home. There's also the risk that some students would find it dull and simply switch off. That said, weighing it all up, I still come down firmly on the side of teaching it. The way I see it, the benefits far outweigh the drawbacks. Even a handful of lessons on budgeting and saving could set young people up for life and save them from learning the hard way. At the end of the day, an education that ignores something as fundamental as money is, in my opinion, missing a trick.

Investitsiyalar, qarzlar va byudjetlashtirish kabi narsalar haqida erta bilib olish orqali ular hayotda keyinchalik yuzaga kelishi mumkin bo'lgan muammolardan qochishlari mumkin. Biroq, allaqachon to'lib toshgan o'quv dasturini ortiqcha yuklamasdan buni qanday amalga oshirishni ko'rib chiqish va o'qitish usullari talabalar uchun qiziqarli va dolzarb bo'lishini ta'minlash muhim.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The proposition to integrate financial literacy into the core academic curriculum is highly relevant today. Advocates passionately insist that teaching students how to manage money is vitally necessary to prevent future poverty. By learning practical skills like budgeting, understanding debt, and navigating taxes early on, teenagers are effectively equipped for the harsh economic realities of adult life. Supporters argue schools must teach them not just how to earn, but how to stay "in the black."
Conversely, opponents present several pragmatic objections. They highlight that the current syllabus is already dangerously overcrowded, placing immense pressure on students. Furthermore, critics argue that financial management is inherently a personal, family matter that should be taught by parents, not standardized by bureaucrats. Finally, complex taxation lessons might simply bore teenagers, rendering the classes entirely ineffective.
In conclusion, ignorance of finance ruins lives. While the curriculum is tight, dedicating even minor resources to basic economic survival skills is undoubtedly a worthwhile investment in society's future.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Moliyaviy savodxonlikni asosiy o'quv dasturiga kiritish taklifi bugungi kunda juda dolzarbdir. Himoyachilar talabalarga pulni qanday boshqarishni o'rgatish kelajakdagi qashshoqlikning oldini olish uchun juda zarur ekanligini qat'iy ta'kidlaydilar. O'smirlar byudjetlashtirish, qarzni tushunish va soliqlar bilan erta shug'ullanish kabi amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rganib, kattalar hayotining shafqatsiz iqtisodiy voqeliklariga samarali tayyorlanadilar. Tarafdorlar maktablar ularga nafaqat pul topishni, balki "qora ro'yxatda" qolishni ham o'rgatishi kerakligini ta'kidlaydilar.

Aksincha, opponentlar bir nechta amaliy e'tirozlarni keltiradilar. Ular hozirgi o'quv dasturi allaqachon juda to'lib-toshganligini va talabalarga juda katta bosim o'tkazayotganini ta'kidlaydilar. Bundan tashqari, tanqidchilarning ta'kidlashicha, moliyaviy boshqaruv mohiyatan shaxsiy, oilaviy masala bo'lib, uni byurokratlar tomonidan standartlashtirilmasdan, ota-onalar o'rgatishi kerak. Nihoyat, murakkab soliq darslari shunchaki o'smirlarni zeriktirishi va darslarni butunlay samarasiz qilishi mumkin.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, moliya sohasidagi jaholat hayotni buzadi. O'quv dasturi zich bo'lsa-da, asosiy iqtisodiy omon qolish ko'nikmalariga hatto kichik resurslarni ajratish ham, shubhasiz, jamiyat kelajagiga qilingan arzirli sarmoyadir.
